To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the average transverse impact parameters in pp collisions with a given hard parton-partonic process are much smaller than in minimum bias collisions, that these impact parameters are very weakly dependent on the transverse momentum of the parton (jet) produced in such collisions, and that these impact parameters govern the transverse multiplicities in such events.

(i) the transverse spatial structure of the nucleon is a key ingredient in determining the p_T of the parton (jet) in a high-energy hard parton-parto n process; (ii) the transverse multiplicities of events with a hard part on - parton interaction are very small, and can be used to identify the p_T range where the hard processes dominate.

the impact parameter distribution in pp collisions with a given hard process depends only weakly on the transverse momentum of the produced partons, and that the transverse multiplicities in such events depend on the impact parameters, which in turn are governed by the impact parameter distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transverse structure of nucleons.
the transverse spatial distributions of nucleons and partons in nucleons.
the study of the transverse spatial distributions of partons and their implications for hard parton-partons processes in pp collisions at the LHC.

the proposed method is a very promising tool for the LHC physics programme.

the transverse multiplicities in the direction perpendicular to a trigger jet or particle in hard processes at high p_T are much lower than in minimum-bias collisions, and they do not depend much on p_T of the trigger jet.
, if a hard parton is produced in a high-p_T event, it is likely to be accompanied by a number of other particles with transverse momenta p_T ~ 1 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact parameter distribution for a given hard scattering process is a unique function of the transverse momentum of the produced partons.
we provide an alternative to the traditional method to determine the minimum p_T in hard processes at LHC by using information on the impact parameter distribution.
we provide a method to determine the transverse momentum scale for the transition of particle production in high energy pp collisions from soft to hard parton-partonic processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hard parton-partons processes are expected to dominate particle production at transverse momenta as low as 2-5 GeV in the central rapidity region of pp collisions at LHC.
the transverse spatial distributions of partons in the proton and the impact parameters of pp collisions are crucial for understanding the origin of particle production at LHC.

the transverse multiplicities of high-p_T particles in pp collisions are very sensitive to the transverse structure of the colliding protons, which in turn can be probed via hard exclusive processes in deep inelastic scattering.
